answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period before it may vote on reputation or receive work. The protocol caps each stake’s influence and lets peers slash it when a provable fraud claim succeeds, so splitting funds across many names does not multiply voting power. A sybil attacker must therefore acquire and immobilize real capital, risking loss and opportunity cost; ivory, saffron, and nadir can be ordinary agent names, not extra identities with free influence.
